title: Chikungunya cases in Germany and the Czech Republic from 2010–2026 – a multicenter, retrospective Analysis
summary:
Except for the evaluation of a small cohort of returning travelers with Chikungunya from 2007 and individual case reports, no analysis of Chikungunya cases in Germany has been published to our knowledge (Taubitz, Winfried et al., 2007). The risk of an increase in Chikungunya cases and thus the disease burden from acute and chronic courses is considered high for Europe due to the increasing spread of the vectors (Heitmann, Anna et al., 2018). 

The aim of this multicenter study is the retrospective, descriptive evaluation of routine clinical data of Chikungunya cases from Infectious disease and Rheumatology centers in Germany from 2010–2026. Particular attention will be paid to the disease burden of chronic cases.

interventions.name: Retrospective, descriptive analysis of the epidemiology, diagnostics, clinical presentation, disease burden, therapy, and course of Chikungunya cases from the participating Infectious disease and Rheumatology centers in Germany and the Czech Republic from 2010–2026

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Age ≥ 18 years
• Clinical presentation and epidemiology (stay in an endemic area) consistent with acute, subacute, or chronic Chikungunya infection
• Virological findings consistent with acute (CHIKV-PCR positive and/or anti-CHIKV-IgM positive), subacute (anti-CHIKV-IgM/IgG positive), or chronic Chikungunya infection (anti-CHIKV-IgG positive, titer increase)
Exclusion criteria:
• Age < 18 years
